title: Outer membrane and Whole cell proteome Analysis of tamA, tamB and tamAB knockout mutants compared to the wildtype
projectDescription: The Translocation and Assembly Module (TAM), composed of TamA and TamB, facilitates the insertion of some β-barrel proteins into the OM of Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae, and has also been implicated in lipid homeostasis. However, its role in Pseudomonas aeruginosa remains mostly uncharacterized. To investigate TAM’s function and drug target potential in P. aeruginosa, we generated both single gene knockouts and the tamAB double knockout and isolated outer membrane proteins (OMP) and whole cell lysate (WCP) and run mass spectrometry.
sampleProcessingProtocol: Outer membrane isolation was performed following the protocol as described by Leo et al 2015 with some adjustments. Briefly, bacteria were inoculated into 500 ml of LB and grown overnight at 37º C with shaking at 180 rpm. An amount of bacteria corresponding to 500 ml at an optical density at 600 nm (OD600nm) of 1.0 was pelleted for 10 minutes at 5000x g. The pellet was washed with 20 ml 10 mM HEPES buffer at pH 7.4 and then resuspend in 10 ml of 10 mM HEPES, to which 0.1 mg/ml lysozyme, MgCl2 and MnCl2 to 10 mM and DNase I at 10 µg/ml were added. The cells were then lysed by sonicating on ice on Soniprep 150 plus. The lysates were then centrifuged at 5000 × g for 10 minutes (supernatant collected here as whole lysate). OMP isolation followed transferring the supernatant to an SS-34 tube and centrifuged for 30 min at 25 000 x g. The supernatant was decanted, and the pellet resuspended in 2 ml of 10 mM HEPES at pH 7.4 in addition to 2 ml of 2% (w/v) N-lauroyl sarcosine. The inner membranes were subsequently solubilized at room temperature (RT) with agitation for 30 min. The Thermo Scientific Pierce BCA Protein Assay Kit was used to quantify proteins and 50 ug sent for mass spectrometry. Four replicates (n=4) of each sample were used.
dataProcessingProtocol: Raw data files were processed using DIA-NN (version 1.8.2), with a Pseudomonas aeruginosa SwissProt FASTA database (Sept 2024), enabling library-free search and deep learning-based spectra prediction for library generation. Analysis against the predicted peptide library was carried out with match between runs on. Labelfree quantification was performed at a precursor FDR of 1.0%, with default DIA-NN parameters unless otherwise specified. Output from the DIA-NN pg_matrix file was further processed using LIMMA via the AMICA 3.0.1 R based software platform for analysis of proteomics data to generate protein differential expression for downstream analysis, with a min-based imputation, Log2FC >0.6, <-0.6 and adjusted p-value of 0.05.
